title: Their teaching: all events, even free and contingent ones, are decreed by an absolute, energetic decree that cannot fail
source_text: XXV. Nempe haec est eorum doctrina, Absoluto & energetico ut loquuntur Dei decreto quaecunque fiunt a causis etiam liberis & contingentibus decreta & ordinata esse. Hoc decretum nunquam irritum esse posse, sed omnino necesse esse ut impleantur quae sic a Deo decreta sunt. Adeoque illa ipsa quae causae contingentes & liberae operantur, hujus decreti respectu necessario fieri nec aliter evenire posse.
pass_a_gloss: XXV. Namely this is their doctrine, That by an Absolute and energetic decree of God, as they speak, whatever things are done by causes even free and contingent, have been decreed and ordered. That this decree can never be void, but that it is altogether necessary that the things so decreed by God be fulfilled. And so that those very things which contingent and free causes work, are necessarily done in respect of this decree, nor can come out otherwise.
pass_b_english: Their teaching is this. By an absolute and, as they call it, 'energetic' decree of God, whatever is done even by free and contingent causes has been decreed and ordered. This decree can never fail, and what God has so decreed must without exception be fulfilled.
So the very things that contingent and free causes do are done necessarily with respect to this decree, and cannot turn out otherwise.

choices.why: The Reformed scholastics' Greek-derived term for God's operative decree, divided into effective and permissive; kept as their term.
